description:
For millions of people in Britain, everyday actions such as boiling an egg, making tea or turning on the heating are getting more expensive. From Thursday, the price cap on a typical household’s annual gas and electricity bill rises from £2,200 to about £2,280 – an £80 increase, roughly £7 a month, a 4% jump. The main driver is the war in the Middle East, which has pushed up gas prices across global markets.
Some UK consumers who fixed their tariffs have delayed the impact, and the government has tried to cushion the blow by removing VAT from electricity bills and maintaining a regulatory price cap on what suppliers can charge per unit. But many households say it is nowhere near enough.

Al Jazeera's Rory Challands reports from London.

description:
China is rapidly integrating artificial intelligence into everyday life, from robot baristas and delivery services to traffic management, healthcare and education. AI algorithms increasingly recommend what people watch and buy, assign delivery orders and help match passengers with drivers. Generative AI is also becoming widely used for research, writing, translation and other daily tasks, with about 602 million users in China at the end of last year. That was more than double the number recorded a year earlier and represented about 43 percent of the population. Surveys suggest Chinese people are generally more receptive to AI despite concerns about its risks. Beijing is now seeking to expand its use through its AI Plus strategy, including in homes, consumer technology, healthcare and elderly care. The next stage will see AI move beyond answering questions to carrying out tasks on behalf of users. 

Al Jazeera’s Katrina Yu reports from Beijing, China.

Families in Gaza have buried the remains of 105 Palestinians recovered nearly three years after they were killed in an Israeli attack on Gaza City. The victims were killed when the seven-storey al-Taj 3 residential building and nearby buildings in the al-Yarmouk neighbourhood were destroyed by Israeli air strikes in October 2023. Gaza's Civil Defence says an estimated 7,000 people are still trapped beneath rubble across the Strip, with heavy machinery and international assistance needed to recover them. For families, the recovery of the remains provides long-awaited closure, but thousands are still waiting to learn the fate of their loved ones. One family member said 37 relatives, including his wife, four children, parents and siblings, were killed in the attack. The recovery of the 105 bodies is one of the largest such operations since the war began and could take years to complete. 

Al Jazeera's Ibrahim Khalili reports from Gaza City.

description: Pakistan says it carried out air strikes on armed-group targets in Afghanistan's southern Helmand province, killing 22 fighters and destroying weapons and ammunition storage facilities. Afghanistan's government says civilian homes were hit, killing nine women and children and injuring 11 others. The strikes come amid a rise in cross-border violence, with Pakistan accusing armed groups based in Afghanistan of carrying out attacks on its territory. In Pampanga province, Aeta farming communities who have cultivated the crop for generations now face pressure as export demand grows. The Philippine government has restricted fresh ube exports to protect local supply, after reports that farmers were depleting stocks meant for future planting seasons. For the Aeta, the boom raises questions about who benefits when a traditional staple becomes a global commodity.

Al Jazeera’s Jamela Alindogan reports from Pampanga province, northern Philippines.
